testo: Fast aircraft and drones: a collision, an engine failure, a flash that blinds the cameras.
When the view is lost, what should the screen say?
MoVi declares what it has not observed.
Three answers per track.
I see it.
I don't see it, but here is where it can be.
Or: I don't know.
In six flight scenarios, MoVi never said clear where an aircraft, a drone or a fragment was.
An engine fails at a hundred and thirty-five metres per second.
MoVi infers the event and declares the cameras unreliable within one second, in sixty of sixty simulated runs.
Low-energy debris stays inside the declared volume in fifty-eight of sixty.
Two fast drones collide.
MoVi warns of the close pass at least ten seconds ahead, in sixty of sixty runs.
The collision is not yet declared as an event, but the region is kept: the fragments stayed inside it in every simulated run.
A flash blinds every optical sensor.
Radar alone keeps a region for every track, and identity is presumed.
When continuity is lost, MoVi computes, in the motion model, how confidence falls, and grows the region to keep nine chances in ten.
On public flight tracks, with a simulated sensor, the region held the aircraft eighty-five to eighty-nine times in a hundred, from one to thirty seconds.
In turns, seventy-three: a declared limit.
Now MoVi rides on a drone, keeping the track of a fast drone ahead.
Nearby, two drones collide: flash, smoke, debris.
The cameras are declared unreliable.
In sixty of sixty simulated runs, the tracked drone stayed inside its region, and no fragment was ever called clear.
Even with the radar blinded for up to two seconds, MoVi never called a fragment clear.
The same core works on a site: a drone behind a building, warned in time in two hundred of two hundred runs.
And at short range: people, cars, trains.
The limits: everything is simulated, with no physical sensor, and classes are labelled by hand.
Next: a contact rule for fast collisions, state-of-the-art sensors, dedicated hardware, field trials.
MoVi observes and warns.
By SDMs.
